newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH SEASON MAY BE BROUGHT FORWARD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH SEASON MAY BE BROUGHT FORWARD.

text.p: The next English soccer season may be brought forward to avoid fixture congestion prior to the 1998 World Cup finals in France.
The Football League is hoping to start a week early on August 9 next year, while the premier league is believed to favour kicking off earlier still, on August 2.

Officials of the two competitions are talking with the Football Association, partly to avoid a repeat of the increasing number of postponements brought about this season by overseas players required for international duty.
An early start would also allow enough free dates for England coach Glenn Hoddle to claim players for training sessions.
There would be problems if next season began on the same weekend as a World Cup qualifying programme scheduled for August 16. Many games would have to be called off.
